title: A super El Nino is coming

scenes.title: SUPER EL NINO
vo: The Pacific Ocean is running a fever.
And it could become the strongest El Niño since 1950.

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: Normally, trade winds push warm water west, toward Asia.
Cold water rises up to replace it.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: In El Niño, those winds weaken.
The warm water sloshes back east, toward the Americas.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: Right now, part of the Pacific is two point one degrees above normal.
NOAA expects it to stay strong into early twenty twenty-seven.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: The northern US often gets warmer and drier.
The Gulf Coast and Southeast get wetter.

scenes.title: BONUS
vo: Fun fact: fishermen named it in the sixteen hundreds.
It peaked near Christmas, so they called it El Niño. The little boy.
